name: Residence Visa by Family Unity (Unidad Familiar)

requirement_groups.name: Sponsor is a Mexican citizen or permanent resident

requirements.blocker_text: Eligible relatives of a Mexican-citizen or permanent-resident sponsor: spouse or common-law partner (5+ years cohabitation, or any duration if there are children together), parents, minor/dependent children (including stepchildren and wards), and, for Mexican-citizen or permanent-resident sponsors specifically, minor/dependent siblings.

requirement_groups.name: Sponsor is a temporary resident or temporary student resident

outcome_override.duration_length: matches the sponsor's own temporary resident permit

requirements.blocker_text: Eligible relatives of a temporary-resident or temporary-student-resident sponsor: spouse or common-law partner (5+ years cohabitation, or any duration if there are children together), parents, and minor/dependent children (including stepchildren and wards) -- siblings do NOT qualify under a temporary-resident sponsor.

evidence_required.document: Sponsor's valid ID or residency card
Birth/marriage certificate proving the family relationship
Proof of dissolution of any prior marriage, if applicable

outcome.duration_length: variable by sponsor group (see requirement_groups outcome_override)

sources.title: Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM) -- Visa por unidad familiar: eligible relatives and resulting residence status by sponsor type

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Mexico's initial build. TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT OUTCOMES modelled as OR-logic groups within the SAME visa (family unity), using outcome_override since the resulting residence status differs by sponsor type per the tier-1 source: family of a Mexican citizen or permanent resident get PERMANENT residence directly (no temporary-then-upgrade step), while family of a temporary/student resident get a temporary permit matching the sponsor's own validity. This is a genuinely favourable, direct-to-permanent family route distinct from the general family_reunification-style routes seen in other countries' builds. work_rights conservatively set to 'none' at the route level (the source did not confirm work rights either way); note this may be overly conservative particularly for the permanent-residence outcome group, where Mexican permanent residents generally do have work rights -- flagged rather than asserted.
